title: High-Protein Chicken Teriyaki Stir-Fry
description: A quick 25-minute chicken teriyaki stir-fry packed with tender chicken breast and crisp vegetables in a savory homemade sauce. This balanced meal delivers 38 grams of protein per serving and works great for quick weeknight dinners.

ingredients.item: boneless skinless chicken breasts, cut into bite-sized pieces

steps: Whisk soy sauce, honey, rice vinegar, ginger, and garlic together in a small bowl to make the teriyaki sauce. Whisk the cornstarch and cold water separately in a small dish to create a slurry.

Heat 1/2 tablespoon of avocado oil in a 12-inch skillet over medium-high heat for 2 minutes until shimmering. Add the chicken pieces in a single layer and cook undisturbed for 4 minutes until golden brown on the bottom.

Flip the chicken and cook for another 3 to 4 minutes until an internal temperature of 165°F (74°C) is reached and the chicken is no longer pink inside. Remove the chicken from the skillet and set aside on a clean plate.

Add the remaining 1/2 tablespoon of avocado oil to the same skillet over medium-high heat. Add the broccoli florets and sliced bell pepper, stir-frying for 4 minutes until crisp-tender and vibrant green.
Pour the teriyaki sauce into the skillet with the vegetables and bring to a simmer over medium heat.
Give the cornstarch slurry a quick stir, then pour it into the simmering sauce, stirring constantly for 1 to 2 minutes until thickened and glossy.

Return the cooked chicken and any resting juices back into the skillet, tossing everything together for 1 minute until heated through and fully coated in the sauce. Remove from heat and serve warm over cooked jasmine rice.
tips: Cut the chicken into uniform bite-sized pieces so they cook evenly and quickly.
Swap jasmine rice for cauliflower rice to adjust the carbohydrate content if desired.
Store leftovers in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3 days.
storage: Store in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3 days. Reheat in a skillet over medium heat until steaming hot.

steps_short: Whisk soy sauce, honey, vinegar, ginger, and garlic together.
Sear chicken breast pieces in a hot skillet until golden.
Cook broccoli and bell peppers until crisp and tender.
Simmer the teriyaki sauce and thicken with cornstarch.
Toss the chicken and veggies back into the glossy glaze.

issues: Teriyaki sauce ratio lacks umami depth (traditionally includes mirin or sake, though soy sauce and honey work for a simple stir-fry variation).

The cornstarch slurry amount (1 tsp cornstarch to 1 tbsp water) is too low to properly thicken 1/3 cup of soy sauce plus added moisture from vegetables; standard practice is at least 1 tbsp cornstarch for this liquid volume.
Adding the sauce directly to the pan before the slurry risks burning the honey and high sodium reduction before thickening.
